findings.summary: Live effect on the proposed-job queue is not stated: proposed requests whose stored reading omits a bullet will drop out of the drain.
findings.evidence: steward.rs:419-428: for a Proposed job, `queued_work` returns None when `check_reading_text(latest, &request.text)` is not Accept ('left out until a person runs `athena go`'). The plan analyses only the steward.rs test fixture, not the queued requests already stored with readings that this check now refuses. Fix: State in the CHANGELOG entry and the dependents reason that proposed requests whose stored reading omits an Acceptance bullet are held out of the drain until `athena go` or a re-read, and that this is intended.
findings.location: Dependents: 'gate result for a reading plus request' (steward.rs queued_work)

findings.summary: Unweighted share lets generic domain words count as cover, so the check is weak where bullets share framing or common words.
findings.evidence: The plan's own bp5e estimate is 3 of 7 stems (about 43%) against a threshold of 35. A bullet such as 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' (stems: test, fail, chang, pass) reaches 50% from any criterion that has 'test' and 'pass'. The framing-only criterion 'The status list shows jobs' covers every sibling (Risks 2). Fix: Keep the design but print, in the tuning table, which stems matched each bullet, so a cover made only of framing or generic words is visible. Optionally add a short list of Athena-generic words (test, pass, cargo, change, job, reading) to the stop list and re-tune from the table. Do not reintroduce rare-stem zeroing.

findings.summary: The sibling bullets for ttnw and bp5e are rebuilt by the planner, and the claim rule's outcome depends on them, so the tuning can fit its own fixtures.
findings.evidence: The ttnw example passes only because 'test' appears in b1 and not in the rebuilt sibling b2. The plan says only the quoted strings are verbatim and that records/ is absent. Fix: Add a second rebuilt sibling variant for each of ttnw and bp5e in which the sibling also contains 'test' (or the shared distinguishing word), and assert the outcome either way. That shows whether acceptance depends on how the sibling was worded. Keep the 'rebuilt, records absent' labels.

findings.summary: Permission matching misses some wordings, though only on the safe side.
findings.evidence: `sentences` (checks.rs:332) splits at newlines but not at '?', and `has_phrase` matches exact spacing. So a hard-wrapped 'You may split\nthis job' is not matched, and 'Should we split? You may split this job.' falls in one sentence with a '?'. Both leave the check on. Fix: Collapse white space within each paragraph before splitting into sentences, and add one wrapped-permission row to the phrase table.

findings.summary: The fake reader's local Acceptance parse can drift from coverage.rs's wrapped-bullet joining.
findings.evidence: athena-agent cannot depend on athena-core (crate reach), so the plan writes a second small parser in fake.rs. Fix: Have the fake copy the whole text from each bullet line up to the next bullet, blank line or heading, so a wrapped bullet still scores 100. Add a fake.rs test with a wrapped bullet.

summary: The plan fits the accepted reading. Each bullet's score is the share of its own content stems found in its best criterion, no prose-repeated word is dropped, a criterion that omits the bullet is refused with the bullet named, a split counts only when the request affirmatively allows one, and the check is one step! line. I checked the code the plan relies on and it exists as described: `refusing_check` and its step order (checks.rs:518-546), `sentences` (checks.rs:332), `has_phrase` (surveys.rs:39), `is_bullet` and `request_text_acceptance` (topics.rs:266/276), the glob re-exports in reading.rs:58-72, both `reading_source()` lists (reading.rs:1491, refusal_corpus.rs:2670), `INPUT_FORMS: [&str; 52]`, `base_reading`, `case()`, `cases()`, and in replay.rs `replay_declaration`, `replay_limit_percent` and `check_reading_text`. The verification replay over recorded readings that the plan leans on is real (run/mod.rs:2225). The corpus cases in `cases()` only push criteria or change a criterion's kind; none replaces the criteria. So with `base_reading` copying every bullet, the replay assertion that no other case is refused by the new check holds. The new claim rule is a targeted, deterministic fix for the shared-framing failure. The plan states and pins its known limits: a framing-only criterion slips through, and a merged paraphrase is refused. I found no blocker or major problem. Four minor or nit points: the live effect on `steward::queued_work` is not stated; plain unweighted share lets generic domain words count as cover; the claim rule is tuned on sibling bullets the planner rebuilt; and the fake reader's local bullet parse may drift from the check's parser. A few edge cases in the split-permission matching are all on the safe side.
